own_scenes.desc: En la primavera de 1966 Warhol era el artista más famoso de Estados Unidos y ya no hacía arte en el sentido tradicional: había anunciado en 1965 que dejaba la pintura por el cine, la gente y los entornos totales. La Factory de la calle 47 Este era a la vez cadena de producción de serigrafías, plató y escenario abierto; un espejo de la sociedad neoyorquina donde lo que esta despreciaba (drag queens, yonquis, chaperos, perturbados) podía volverse superstar. Sus cuadros devolvían a América sus valores (sexo, muerte, crimen, fama, dinero, producción en masa) y sus series de desastres el regodeo mediático en la muerte. Obrero gay de Pittsburgh con una rabia de outsider, se convirtió en estrella de rock en el caos de su retrospectiva de Filadelfia (octubre de 1965). Gloria Steinem lo puso en el centro de la cultura pop en Life y Susan Sontag hizo de lo camp una obsesión; Batman, A Clockwork Orange, el caso de los asesinatos de Tucson y Capote alimentaban el aire de violencia que él recortaba de las revistas. Con la anfetamina el ambiente se volvió paranoico y cruel; Danny Williams, su amante y autor de las luces del EPI, desapareció en julio. Durante 1966, sin pretenderlo, «se convirtió en América».

refs.q: Warhol was very taken with the song and suggested that, when it was cut as a single, the last phrase should be repeated as a locked groove.
refs.para: ‘I’ll Be Your Mirror’ was written during the very first few months of the Velvet Underground’s involvement at the Factory, and it reflected the febrile atmosphere. Warhol was very taken with the song and suggested that, when it was cut as a single, the last phrase should be repeated as a locked groove. Clearly, it was an idea that resonated with him: ‘I’ll be your mirror / Reflect what you are / In case you don’t know.’
refs.chapter: Junio: I’ll Be Your Mirror: la Velvet Underground y la América de Warhol

refs.q: Behind Warhol’s impenetrable facade lurked an outsider’s fury.
refs.para: Behind Warhol’s impenetrable facade lurked an outsider’s fury. As a working-class gay man from the deepest Rust Belt, he had an incredible drive to assimilate – to crash the glamour world of metropolitan society, inherited wealth and artistic fame. Suffering serial humiliations and setbacks, he played the game until the point, sometime in the early sixties, when he began to achieve his goal. Then, for a brief period, he rewrote the rules. His underlying rage came out.
refs.chapter: Junio: I’ll Be Your Mirror: la Velvet Underground y la América de Warhol

refs.q: Warhol’s high 1960s paintings and silk screens reflected the country’s dominant values back at America
refs.para: Warhol’s high 1960s paintings and silk screens reflected the country’s dominant values back at America: sex, death, crime, celebrity, media, money, mass production. Just as the mirror works with psychology, the response to these works changed with the individual gaze. Contemporary critics were divided, if not actively hostile. Were they a put-on? Were they a critique? Were they a wish fulfilment? Or were they just there?
refs.chapter: Junio: I’ll Be Your Mirror: la Velvet Underground y la América de Warhol

refs.q: This was his peak. Almost unconsciously, certainly without stated intent, he became America.
refs.para: Like the mirror, Warhol was plastic and multiphrenic, deceptively seductive yet icily dispassionate. As he told Gretchen Berg, ‘The artificial fascinates me, the bright and shiny.’ During 1966, he was in tune with the times – their profound confusion, escalating violence and sheer mediated frenzy – in a way that he never had been before and never would be again. This was his peak. Almost unconsciously, certainly without stated intent, he became America.
refs.chapter: Junio: I’ll Be Your Mirror: la Velvet Underground y la América de Warhol

refs.q: Warhol was both terrified and thrilled. He had become a rock star.
refs.para: Warhol was both terrified and thrilled. He had become a rock star. ‘I’d seen kids scream over Elvis and the Beatles and the Stones – rock idols and movie stars – but it was incredible to think of it happening at an ART opening. Even a Pop Art opening. But then, we weren’t just AT the art exhibit – we WERE the art exhibit, we were the art incarnate and the sixties were really about people, not about what they did; “the singer/not the song” etc.
refs.chapter: Junio: I’ll Be Your Mirror: la Velvet Underground y la América de Warhol
